facts.title: AI is the New OS
facts.value: Work is shifting from clicking through application interfaces to agents using command-line tools and MCP servers, so technology leaders should prioritise agent governance, agent-addressable systems and shorter vendor contracts.
facts.evidence: The operating system, as we have known it for forty years, is being quietly replaced.

facts.title: State of the CIO, 2026: CIOs set the course for AI ROI
facts.value: CIOs are moving past open-ended AI experimentation, building structures and KPIs that prioritize use cases with measurable business returns, according to the 2026 State of the CIO survey.

facts.title: Why Enterprises Need a New Playbook for AI Value
facts.value: AI value is hard to prove because ROI measurement, adoption and accountability are failing, not the technology; the fix is outcome-based measures and shared ownership.
facts.evidence: The technology isn't failing. The measurement framework is.
facts.date_evidence: visible byline: Rahul Neel Mani, July 1, 2026

facts.title: Enterprises still chase incremental, not transformational, AI gains
facts.value: Most enterprises still settle for marginal AI productivity gains rather than transformational ones, the piece reports, because process redesign and governance are not yet in place.
facts.evidence: focusing instead on incremental productivity and efficiency gains

facts.title: Employees are doing the work. AI is getting the credit.
facts.value: Managers who assume AI drove the work are delaying promotions and trimming raises for the employees who did it, so credit should follow outcomes, not tools.
